name: Shenzhen Sinexcel Electric Co., Ltd. (深圳市盛弘电气股份有限公司)
employees: ~2,484 (end of FY2024, per aggregator summary of annual report)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Sinexcel's high-margin overseas storage PCS line is the earnings engine over a commoditizing domestic base, with AI data-center power as pre-revenue optionality; the 11 August 2026 H1 report is the near-term checkpoint. BACKGROUND: Sinexcel is a Chinese power-electronics company built around modular power conversion technology, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange ChiNext board since August 2017. It operates four reported business lines: EV charging and battery-swap equipment (its largest segment since 2024), new-energy power conversion (bi-directional energy storage PCS and containerized storage systems), industrial supporting power supplies (active harmonic filters, static var generators, UPS), and battery formation & test equipment. The company claims 5,000+ energy storage projects, 200,000+ EV charging systems, 20,000+ power quality projects, and 300,000+ battery test channels deployed, with manufacturing in Huizhou, Suzhou, California, and Malaysia and subsidiaries across the US, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.
ecosystemRole: We assess Sinexcel as one of China's leading third-party PCS (power conversion system) suppliers for battery energy storage, with grid-forming capability and a fast-growing, high-margin overseas storage business (StellaON platform certified for multiple European grids). Also a merchant supplier of EV DC fast chargers and 20/40 kW charging modules, and a long-established power-quality vendor increasingly levered to AI data-center (AIDC) power demand.

productsAndServices.name: Energy storage PCS & containerized systems
productsAndServices.description: Bi-directional modular storage inverters spanning 30 kW modules to 1,575 kVA utility units and containerized systems: the StellaON 1250K/1575K utility-scale grid-forming flagship (690 Vac, DC 1040-1500 V, 99% peak efficiency), Sirius 135K C&I/microgrid PCS (PWS1-135M), the modular PWS family (PWS2-30P 30 kW DC/AC module; PWS1-500KTL 500 kVA cabinet of up to 8x62.5 kW modules; PWS1-1725KTL-H cabinet of up to 8x215 kVA modules), and 20-ft/40-ft medium-voltage stations up to the 40-ft 10 MW Centralized MV Station (22-33 kV, oil-immersed transformer integrated).
highlights: 500+ MW of StellaON orders secured in H1 2026 ahead of its formal European launch at Intersolar Europe 2026; 15+ active projects across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Africa; first grid connection in Vietnam (April 2026)
Named a BloombergNEF Tier 1 power inverter manufacturer (Q2 2026); claims 17 GW installed across 5,000+ projects in 60+ markets, with 60+ certified models

Grid-forming across the range: VSG/PQ/VF (plus SVG mode on StellaON), black start, 100+ MW off-grid parallel operation; StellaON claims 1.5x overload for 60 s vs ~1.2x industry typical and MTBF >300,000 h
Entered Japan's frequency-regulation market June 2026 (2 MW/8 MWh Matsusaka project on two 1,375 kW PCS; 60+ Japanese utility-scale projects, 10+ local EMS integrations, Tokyo subsidiary)

Grid-code certifications: EN 50549-2/-10, IEC/EN 62477, RfG+PTPIREE (among the first PCS certified for Poland), Finland SJV2024 (160 kW PCS), UL 1741/IEEE 1547 (Sirius 135K, March 2026); FY2025 overseas storage revenue RMB 645M, +50.1% YoY, at a 61.3% gross margin (aggregator figures)
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes as a third-party modular-PCS specialist against integrated-inverter giants (Sungrow, Power Electronics, SMA) by selling conversion hardware to battery integrators and developers rather than competing with them on full BESS supply; differentiation claims are module-parallel architecture, overload headroom (1.5x/60 s), reliability (MTBF >300,000 h, key-component swap <1 h), and breadth of European grid-code certification (early Poland cohort).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to BESS integrators, developers, and EPCs; in Japan through local developers and EMS platforms (Namcha Barwa partnership, June 2026); in the US through Sinexcel Inc. (California)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale BESS developers (Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Japan), C&I storage integrators, wind/solar co-located storage (e.g. Latvia's largest wind-farm BESS on 1725 kW PCS), frequency-regulation and ancillary-services players
productsAndServices.roadmap: Spain and US certifications of StellaON stated as 'coming soon' at the June 2026 launch; company active in drafting grid-forming energy-storage standards (2025 PR)

productsAndServices.name: EV charging & battery-swap equipment
productsAndServices.description: SEC series DC fast chargers from 30 kW to 1,280 kW - integrated (SEC30, SEC80 40-80 kW DC + 22 kW AC, SEC240, SEC640, SEC1000/160) and distributed (SEC480 with up to 6 dispensers; SEC1280 with 960/1280 kW power stacks and up to 16 connectors, 500 A liquid-cooled dual-connector dispensers boostable to 600 A) - plus the IZAR AC charger and SER 20/40 kW merchant charging modules. Largest revenue segment since 2024 (FY2025: RMB 1.496B, 43.2% of revenue).
highlights: Company claims 'world's No.1 in megawatt-level charger sales' (16 years of expertise, per July 2026 Thailand release); SEC1280 was the first megawatt charger with Eichrecht certification

Bangkok's first megawatt supercharging station with ZEEKR and TPM Automotive (July 2026): 960 kW stack, one 700 A liquid-cooled supercharging dispenser plus three 500 A dispensers, two ZEEKR 7X charged 20-80% in 10 minutes; claimed 97% power utilization
Shell Recharge joint innovation lab in Shenzhen (June 2026): ultra-fast charging, cloud scheduling, solar-storage-charging, megawatt heavy-duty charging, AI O&M
One-stop European e-truck charging solution launched July 2026, pairing megawatt chargers with storage and dispatch software for depot vs 45-minute-rest-stop use cases

CharIN core member (V2G-ready architecture); integrated solar-storage-charging-discharging solution shown at RE+ 2024; certifications: CE, UL, UKCA, TR25 (Singapore), RCM (AU/NZ), KC (Korea), Eichrecht (Germany)
productsAndServices.positioning: Both a charger OEM and a merchant module supplier to other charger makers - one of China's top-three EV charger manufacturers (per CharIN) competing internationally with ABB E-mobility, Alpitronic, and Kempower-class DC fast-charging vendors on distributed architecture (dynamic module-level power allocation) and megawatt-class output; module business competes on SiC efficiency and 50-1000 V output breadth
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct charger sales plus CPO/OEM partnerships (Shell Recharge, ZEEKR/TPM 'EV + charger + local partner' model); SER modules sold merchant to third-party charger builders
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Charge-point operators, bus and truck fleet depots, highway charging hubs, automotive-OEM branded stations; Southeast Asia, Europe, and North America highlighted
productsAndServices.roadmap: OCPP 2.0.1 support rollout (from 2025 per SEC1280 page); megawatt heavy-duty truck charging build-out with Shell lab and European e-truck solution; V2G productization via CharIN membership

productsAndServices.name: Power quality solutions
productsAndServices.description: The company's original business (2009 Shenzhen 'Startup Star' prize for its active power filter), with 20,000+ projects deployed: active harmonic filters (BLADE AHF 5-15 A SiC wall/rack units; standard AHF 25-300 A modules; PRO AHF 150 A at 98.5% peak efficiency; SiC-based Ultra AHF), static var generators (standard 30-200 kvar; PRO SVG 100 kvar at 98.5%; Ultra SVG, ASVG, HSVG, 50/100 kvar hot-plug units), AVC-RTS supercapacitor voltage-sag correction (30-2,400 kVA), and modular UPS; marine-certified variants (DNV, RINA, CCS, BV).
highlights: Recognized as a Tier 1 low-voltage power quality supplier (March 2025 PR); growth now driven by AI data-center (AIDC) and semiconductor-fab power demand
AVC-RTS rides through 100% voltage sags (to zero volts) with 2 ms typical response from supercapacitor storage - aimed at semiconductor fabs, precision manufacturing, and AIDC
SiC adoption across the range: BLADE AHF switches at ~50 kHz average (up to 90 kHz) vs ~20 kHz standard series; PRO series cuts heat ~33% vs legacy
productsAndServices.positioning: Specialist active-compensation vendor competing with Schneider Electric (AccuSine), ABB, and Danfoss-class active filter lines on switching frequency (SiC), modular parallelability (unlimited units), and mounting density; AVC-RTS competes with dynamic voltage restorers and mini-UPS approaches on 2 ms response without batteries
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distributors, panel builders, and system integrators plus direct key accounts; marine via classification-certified OEM channels
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Semiconductor fabs, AI data centers, automotive/PCBA/LED manufacturing, commercial buildings, marine vessels
productsAndServices.roadmap: Power-quality portfolio positioned as the beachhead for the AIDC division's data-center power push (AHF/SVG/AVC-RTS already deployed in AIDCs)

productsAndServices.name: AI data-center (AIDC) power
productsAndServices.description: Dedicated AIDC business division established June 2025 to develop HVDC (high-voltage DC) power systems and solid-state transformers (SST) for data centers, building on the company's APF/SVG power-electronics heritage. Current shipping exposure is a 36 kW HVDC rectifier module - third-party reporting says it is supplied to Vertiv, giving indirect NVIDIA-ecosystem exposure - plus power-quality equipment (AHF/SVG/AVC-RTS) already deployed in AIDCs.
highlights: 36 kW HVDC power module claimed at ~100 W/in3 power density vs ~70 W/in3 industry average (aggregator claim)

Own-brand HVDC products remained pre-revenue as of February 2026 (company statement via financial media); aggregator commentary puts AIDC-related revenue at >20% of the FY2025 industrial-power segment with >50% YoY growth
Planned scope per Chinese financial media: cabinet power plus high-voltage-side and low-voltage-side DC microgrid solutions, overseas-market-focused
productsAndServices.positioning: Enters the AI data-center power race as a module/OEM supplier (contrast Megmeet's NVIDIA-named full-chain position and Delta's incumbency) - the wedge is power-quality incumbency in existing data centers and HVDC modules sold through established power-infrastructure OEMs rather than direct hyperscaler design-ins
productsAndServices.soldThrough: OEM module supply (Vertiv per third-party reports); power-quality channels for AHF/SVG/AVC-RTS into data centers
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Cloud service providers and AI enterprises (cooperative relationships claimed, names undisclosed), data-center power-infrastructure OEMs; overseas markets prioritized
productsAndServices.roadmap: HVDC and SST product launches expected 2026 (per May 2025 division announcement); watch H1 2026 report (due Aug 11, 2026) for first AIDC revenue disclosure

productsAndServices.name: Battery formation & test equipment
productsAndServices.description: BTS-series battery formation, grading, and test systems with energy-recycling power electronics for lithium battery manufacturers; 300,000+ test channels in operation. Third-party reporting names CATL, BYD, ATL, and XPeng among customers.
productsAndServices.positioning: Energy-recycling formation/grading power electronics (charge energy fed back rather than burned) sold on channel density and efficiency; competes with Chroma, Hangke, and Neware-class test-equipment vendors
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Lithium-ion cell makers (power, consumer, storage cells); named third-party-reported customers include CATL, BYD, ATL, XPeng

productsAndServices.name: Microgrid & off-grid converters
productsAndServices.description: Grid-forming microgrid conversion hardware and delivery: PWS1-160M-H 160 kVA high-voltage AC module (VSG technology, seamless on/off-grid transfer, FFR/FCR/FCAS grid services, <=15 ms dispatch response, IP66), Sirius 135K in microgrid duty (100+ units off-grid parallel via proprietary comms, 100% unbalanced load), and PWS2-30P 30 kW modules compatible with lead-acid, lithium, sodium-ion batteries and flywheels; asset-backed storage & microgrid offerings delivered through Sinexcel Inc. (California), including a commercial-scale virtual power plant integration with Molecule Systems.
highlights: 160 kW PCS secured Finland SJV2024 grid-services certification (May 2026)
Multi-chemistry DC-side compatibility (incl. sodium-ion and flywheel) hedges battery-technology shifts
productsAndServices.positioning: Modular grid-forming microgrid PCS positioned against string-inverter-derived hybrid offerings on unbalanced-load tolerance, parallel scale (100+ units), and certified grid-services participation
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Microgrid integrators and EPCs; US direct via Sinexcel Inc.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Industrial parks, island/remote-area microgrids, commercial buildings and data-center backup, VPP operators

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess overseas utility PCS is Sinexcel's margin engine — 61.3% FY2025 gross margin on the storage export line versus commoditized domestic pricing, with StellaON grid certifications (Poland, Nordics, Japan) functioning as queue-jumps into tender shortlists. Basis: filings as relayed by broker summaries.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the third-party PCS position benefits from integrator-versus-vertical dynamics: developers seeking non-captive conversion suppliers keep a durable lane open despite vertically integrated giants.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the AI data-center power line (built on the APF/SVG heritage; HVDC modules third-party-reported shipping to Vertiv) is optionality, pre-revenue as of early 2026 — treat AI-exposure claims as forward-looking until revenue is disclosed.
(Moderate confidence) We assess the EV-charging segment — largest since 2024 but lower-margin — is moving up the value chain toward fleet-infrastructure solutions to escape charger commoditization.

metrics.name: Net profit (attributable)
metrics.result: Slight beat — Soochow Securities titled its review "results slightly beat expectations"; another broker called it in-line

periods.commentary: Segments: EV charging RMB 1.216B (+43.0%), energy storage RMB 857M (≈ -6% YoY, 29.6% gross margin), power quality RMB 603M (+13.1%), battery formation & test RMB 296M. Post-results, Soochow cut 2025/2026 profit forecasts to RMB 560M/680M (from 590M/730M) citing overseas storage tariff risk. Dividend: RMB 5.00 per 10 shares (~RMB 156M).

metrics.name: Net profit (attributable)
metrics.expected: ~RMB 511M (start-of-2025 consensus, aggregator-cited); ~RMB 490M after mid-year broker cuts
metrics.result: ~7% below start-of-year consensus; roughly in line with post-cut estimates after the weak storage H1

periods.commentary: Segments: EV charging RMB 1.496B (+23.0%, now 43.2% of revenue), energy storage RMB 825M (-3.7% — H1 down 39% on the domestic price war, sharp H2 recovery), power quality RMB 710M (+17.8%), battery test RMB 343M (+16.0%). Overseas storage revenue RMB 645M (+50.1%) at 61.3% gross margin. Q4 2025 accelerated: revenue +32.5%, profit +25.9%. Sector narrative: "storage stalled; AIDC/data-center power the swing factor." Dividend: RMB 5.00 per 10 shares (RMB 156M, paid May 2026).

periods.commentary: FY2026 analyst consensus: net profit ~RMB 589–600M (+~26% YoY, EPS ~1.88); one cautious independent estimate ~RMB 538M assuming AIDC revenue halves. Ratings found are buy/overweight-type (Soochow, Everbright, Guolian); no sell ratings found. Market cap ~RMB 15.2B in mid-June 2026 (~28× 2026E earnings).
